q: What is the difference between gross pay and net pay?
r: Net pay is gross pay minus taxes and other deductions
Net pay is the take-home amount.
w: Gross pay is net pay minus taxes
Net pay is the amount before any deductions

q: Jordan earns $15 an hour and works 20 hours in a week. What is Jordan's gross pay for the week?
r: 15 dollars times 20 hours is 300 dollars.

q: Which form does a new employee complete so the employer withholds the correct amount of income tax?
r: The W-4 tells the employer how much federal income tax to withhold.
w: The W-2 is the wage and tax statement sent after the year ends.
A 1099 reports income earned outside of regular employment.
The I-9 verifies eligibility to work.

q: Which is a payroll deduction that the law requires?
r: Social Security tax
FICA taxes are withheld from paychecks by law.
w: These apply only to union members.

q: Marcus earns a salary of $36,000 a year and is paid every two weeks, or 26 times a year. About how much is his gross pay per paycheck?
r: 36,000 divided by 26 is about 1,385.
w: This divides by 52, which is weekly pay.

q: Which is a likely result of building more job skills?
r: Higher earning potential
Skills that employers value usually lead to better pay.

q: Which type of income is money earned from assets, such as interest on a savings account, without doing regular work for it?
r: Passive income
Passive income comes from assets rather than from a job.
w: Tips are paid for service work.

q: What is a share of stock?
r: A unit of ownership in a company
Stockholders own a piece of the company.
w: Lending to a company is a bond.

q: What is a bond?
r: A loan to a company or government that pays interest
Bondholders are lenders, not owners.
w: This is a charge, not an investment.

q: Spreading money across many different investments mainly helps reduce:
r: The risk from any single investment
A loss in one holding is offset by others.
w: Diversification does not change tax rules.

q: A $1,000 investment earns 5 percent simple interest per year. How much interest does it earn over 3 years?
r: Simple interest is 1,000 times 5 percent times 3 years.
w: This is one year of interest.
This is the figure for compound interest.
This is the interest plus the original amount.

q: Which investment is generally considered the lowest risk?
r: U.S. Treasury bonds
They are backed by the U.S. government.

q: Which best describes a mutual fund?
r: A pool of money from many investors used to buy many securities
Investors share in the fund's holdings and results.
w: A fund is not a loan.
A fund is an investment product.

q: Why is starting to invest early helpful?
r: Growth has more time to compound
Earlier investing allows returns to earn their own returns.
w: Investments never lose value early on
Investments can lose value at any time.
Taxes are not owed on early investments

q: What does a credit score summarize?
r: How reliably a person has repaid debts
Lenders use it to judge the risk of lending.
w: The balance in a savings account
Savings do not determine a score.
Income is not part of the score.
The interest rate on all loans
Rates are set by lenders using many factors.

q: Which action most helps build a good credit history?
r: Paying bills on time every month
Payment history is the largest factor in credit scores.
w: Using the full limit on every card
High usage can lower a score.
Applying for many new cards at once
Many applications can hurt a score.
Missing a payment now and then

q: A credit card has an APR of 24 percent. What does APR tell you?
r: The yearly cost of borrowing as a percentage
APR is the annual percentage rate charged on balances.
w: The yearly fee for owning the card
The minimum payment is a separate figure.
The limit is a dollar amount.

q: Sam owes $500 on a card with 2 percent monthly interest and makes no payment. About how much interest is added in one month?
r: 2 percent of 500 dollars is 10 dollars.

q: Which habit helps a cardholder avoid paying interest?
r: Paying the full statement balance each month
No interest is charged on purchases when the full balance is paid by the due date.
w: Interest builds on the remaining balance.
Cash advances usually carry fees and interest right away.
Late payments add fees and interest.

q: Which type of lender typically charges the highest interest rates?
r: A payday lender
Short-term payday loans carry very high effective rates.
w: Credit unions tend to offer lower rates.
Federal student loans carry lower fixed rates.

q: Which best describes a secured loan?
r: A loan backed by collateral the lender can claim if the borrower does not repay
Collateral lowers the lender's risk.
w: A loan guaranteed only by a verbal promise
A loan that must be repaid in one day

q: What is insurance?
r: A way to transfer financial risk to a company in return for premiums
Insurance spreads the cost of losses across many policyholders.
w: A savings plan with guaranteed returns
Insurance is not primarily a savings plan.
Insurance does not need to be repaid.

q: What is an insurance deductible?
r: The amount you pay before the insurance begins to pay
A higher deductible usually lowers the premium.
w: The monthly payment to the insurer
The maximum the insurer will pay
A deductible is not a refund.

q: Which kind of insurance covers a person's medical expenses?
r: Health insurance
Health insurance pays part of medical costs.
w: This covers vehicle damage and liability.
This covers belongings and liability for renters.
This pays beneficiaries after a death.

q: Casey chooses a higher deductible on a car insurance policy. What is the most likely effect?
r: A lower premium but more out-of-pocket cost in a claim
Taking on more of the risk lowers the insurer's price.
w: A higher premium and lower cost in a claim
A higher deductible usually changes the price.
Coverage for all damage with no limits
The deductible has no connection to unlimited coverage.

q: Which action reduces the risk of identity theft?
r: Using strong, unique passwords
Strong, different passwords make accounts harder to break into.
w: One breach could expose every account.

q: What does renter's insurance mainly protect?
r: A renter's belongings and liability
It covers a tenant's possessions and certain legal costs.
w: The landlord's policy covers the structure.
That is not covered by renter's insurance.
Insurance does not affect credit scores.

q: Why should people keep an emergency fund?
r: To cover unexpected expenses without borrowing
A cushion prevents small emergencies from becoming debt.
w: Emergency money should be easy to reach and safe.
Planned expenses belong in a separate goal.

q: What is the main purpose of a savings account?
r: To keep money safe and earn interest
Savings accounts hold money and pay a small return.
w: Checking accounts are used for that.
Stocks are bought through a brokerage.

q: Which describes compound interest?
r: Interest earned on both the original deposit and earlier interest
Compounding makes savings grow faster over time.
w: Interest earned only on the original deposit
Interest charged only once at the start
A fee for opening an account

q: A saver deposits $200 at 3 percent simple interest for one year. How much interest is earned?
r: 3 percent of 200 dollars is 6 dollars.
w: This is the interest plus the deposit.

q: Which is the best first step to build an emergency fund?
r: Set a target and transfer a fixed amount automatically each payday
Automatic saving builds the habit and the balance.
w: Wait until you have extra money left over
There may never be extra money.
Put everything into one risky stock
Emergency money should not be at risk.
Spend first and save whatever remains
This rarely leaves anything to save.

q: Which of these is protected by FDIC insurance, within limits?
r: A savings account at an insured bank
FDIC insurance protects deposits at member banks.
w: Shares held in a stock brokerage
Crypto holdings are not FDIC insured.
A personal loan to a friend

q: What does the Rule of 72 estimate?
r: How long it takes money to double at a given interest rate
Divide 72 by the rate to estimate the years to double.
w: The rule has nothing to do with taxes.
It does not estimate retirement age.
The monthly payment on a loan
Loan payments use a different formula.

q: Which is a specific and measurable savings goal?
r: Save $600 for a laptop in six months by setting aside $100 a month
It states an amount, a date and a method.
w: There is no amount or date.

q: What is a budget?
r: A plan for how to use income
A budget compares expected income with planned spending and saving.
w: A list of past debts only
A budget is a personal plan.
It is a plan, not an account.

q: Which of these is a fixed expense?
r: Monthly rent
Rent is the same amount each month.

q: Ana earns $2,000 a month and follows the 50/30/20 rule. How much is set aside for needs?
r: Fifty percent of 2,000 dollars is 1,000 dollars.
w: This adds the needs and wants shares.

q: Which is the best way to compare the price of two cereal boxes of different sizes?
r: Compare the unit price per ounce
Unit price shows the true cost for the same amount.
w: Size alone does not show price.
Choose the one with a popular mascot
A brand name is not a price comparison.

q: What is comparison shopping?
r: Checking prices and features from several sellers before buying
It helps buyers find the best value.
w: Buying the first item you see
The payment method is a different matter.

q: Which habit best helps control impulse buying?
r: Waiting 24 hours before a non-essential purchase
A pause gives time to decide whether you really want it.
w: This can lead to unplanned purchases.

q: Leo has $50 left until payday. He needs lunch money and wants new headphones. How should he prioritize?
r: Cover needs like lunch first, then use anything left on wants
Needs come before wants when money is limited.
w: Wants should not come before needs.
Split the money evenly between both
Put everything on a credit card
This adds debt for a want.
